title: Mark the pace on agent limit meters
head: e6d9c8e1981c
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Scoped Claude session limits never get the pace indicator, and context names can create a false indicator at the last minute
leads.consequence: The Claude collector emits `Fable Session` with an explicit title but no duration; `windowSpanMs` returns zero, so an active model-specific five-hour allowance has no tick or pace text. A valid `Opus 5 (1M context) Session` instead parses as a one-minute allowance: the guard hides its tick while >1 minute remains but falsely displays 50% pace with 30 seconds left, not roughly 99.8% of five hours. Derive the span from the collector's known window kind/duration, not the model name; preserve a separate display title.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus Finding 2 (1M misparse in last minute; scoped Session span 0 is by design); published as Finding 2

leads.summary: Ahead/under text continues to compare against a cached percentage after Claude limit probes fail
leads.consequence: On a failed Claude usage request with an open cached window, collect_limits serves the old percentage; transport failures set retryAdvised and neither transport nor HTTP failures set usageStatusText when a fallback exists. While the panel stays open, nowMs advances every 30 seconds, so pace advances while the used percentage is frozen. A user can be told 'under' or 'on track' based on old usage, without a visible warning that the comparison is stale. Track the measurement time/stale flag in the limit records and avoid a current ahead/under claim for an old reading.
leads.triage: behavioural; Opus follow-up (opus/followup-stale-cache.md, sealed probe) confirmed stale cached percent with no banner for 429/5xx/transport, pre-existing staleness (#10616); published as optional note

leads.summary: Open #7547's Available mode inverts the fill but leaves this pace tick on the used axis
leads.consequence: The two PRs are divergent, not stacked. #7547 explicitly changes the percentage and meter fill to 1 - used in Available mode. A straightforward resolution of their conflicting Meter value lines preserving both features puts the pace tick at elapsed used fraction while the fill represents available fraction. For a 20%-used, 20%-elapsed window the tick appears at the start of an 80%-full available meter rather than at 80%. Resolve by reflecting the pace coordinate when Available is selected, and make the ahead/under wording unambiguous in that mode. As-is their Panel.qml merge has a conflict at the Meter value/pace binding (the other PR is CONFLICTING against quattro).
leads.triage: corroborates Opus related-PR note on #7547 Available mode; published in Related open PRs

leads.summary: The new pace test passes even when the tick is always invisible
leads.consequence: The helper tests and regex only assert that `pace: root.paceFor(limitRow.window)` appears in source; they do not check the tick's `visible` predicate (or reset text). A plausible broken implementation changing `visible: meter.pace >= 0` to `visible: false` passes all six new assertions while making the feature invisible for every provider. Add an assertion on the Rectangle visibility or a command-only/Qt Quick rendering check and verify the reset text separately.
leads.triage: factual, confirmed from diff (test checks helpers and binding regex only); overlaps Opus untested-inline-logic optional note, merged into it

leads.summary: Open #13770 replaces LimitRow with CompactLimit, leaving the new pace binding without a consumer
leads.consequence: #13770 moves every displayed limit to CompactLimit/Meter and removes the current LimitRow; its meter takes `value` and `markers`, not a `pace` argument, and the exact record-shape test it adds omits spanMs. Its head diverges from this PR and a source merge has seven Panel.qml conflicts. A resolution keeping #13770's page without adding pace to CompactLimit removes the feature; a resolution keeping this PR's spanMs needs to update #13770's deep-equality tests. Port pace into the new meter and tooltip, adjust scoped rows and tests before merging both. This is a cross-PR integration lead, not a claim that the unreconciled tree runs.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus #13770 note (rechecked by Opus at moved head 38db762); published in Related open PRs

leads.summary: Open #11367's unlimited limit rows would receive a fabricated pace comparison
leads.consequence: #11367 emits an `unlimited: true` Minimax weekly window with percent=0 and a real reset time, and its panel explicitly displays `Unlimited` instead of `0%`. If both PRs are reconciled by keeping spanMs and unlimited in the normalized record, paceFor computes an elapsed fraction and resetText says, for example, `pace 50% (-50 under)` under an unlimited meter. There is no finite allowance or meaningful 'under pace' for that row. Suppress the pace tick and ahead/under text for unlimited records, preserving their flag through normalization. Its head and this one diverge and merge-file finds a limitWindow conflict, so this concerns their combined feature, not a running merged tree.
leads.triage: cross-PR combination with #11367 unlimited rows; only relevant if both merged with conflict resolution; dropped

leads.summary: Open localization PRs #7434 and #11010 conflict with this reset-line rewrite
leads.consequence: Both #7434 and #11010 replace the original reset string with `I18n.tr("Resets in %1", [...])`; their Spanish and Chinese catalogs respectively contain that key. The new `"Resets in " + duration + " · pace ..."` is outside that translation call. The PR heads diverge and the same source hunk conflicts, so both cannot merge unchanged; on resolution, render a translatable complete pace line (including ahead/under/on-track variants), rather than discarding the localized reset line or appending untranslated text.
leads.triage: cross-PR localization conflict with #7434/#11010; low value, textual conflict resolves at merge; dropped

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** In `agent-usage-claude-limits-test.sh`, the added node block masks the first one's failures.

### Record-shape test failures now exit 0

The file lacks `set -euo pipefail`, so the appended pace block now sets its exit status. Impact: `./test/shell` passes the file even when the record-shape assertions edited for `spanMs` print `not ok`.

**Suggested change:** Add `set -euo pipefail` after the shebang, per `docs/testing.md`; the head passes with it.

<details><summary>Reproducer (not ok but exit 0 at e6d9c8e)</summary>

Run from a checkout of the PR head (`e6d9c8e1981cf11d832844ed0bfce84635627bd0`) with `node`, `jq` and `python3` available.

Break only what the first `run_node_test` block checks (the title of an untitled weekly window). `paceFor()` is left alone:

```bash
sed -i 's/if (windowIsLong(text)) return "Weekly"/if (windowIsLong(text)) return "Week"/' shell/plugins/agents/Panel.qml
bash test/shell.d/agent-usage-claude-limits-test.sh 2>&1 | grep -E '^not ok|draw the pace tick'; echo "exit=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
```

Actual output:

```
not ok - agents panel still reads a window out of a label that carries no title
ok - agents limit meters draw the pace tick
exit=0
```

Then add the header that `docs/testing.md` gives every shell test, and run it again:

```bash
sed -i '1a set -euo pipefail' test/shell.d/agent-usage-claude-limits-test.sh
bash test/shell.d/agent-usage-claude-limits-test.sh 2>&1 | grep -E '^not ok|draw the pace tick'; echo "exit=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
```

Actual output:

```
not ok - agents panel still reads a window out of a label that carries no title
exit=1
```

Control: on an unmodified PR head, the same `sed -i '1a set -euo pipefail'` header still passes:

```bash
sed -i '1a set -euo pipefail' test/shell.d/agent-usage-claude-limits-test.sh
bash test/shell.d/agent-usage-claude-limits-test.sh 2>&1 | tail -3; echo "exit=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
```

Actual output:

```
ok - agents pace is hidden without a reset time
ok - agents pace is hidden when the parsed span is shorter than the reset
ok - agents limit meters draw the pace tick
exit=0
```
</details>

### Misparse guard fails in a window's last minute

For a scoped label like `Opus 5 (1M context) Session`, `windowSpanMs()` reads `1M` as one minute, so in the last 60 s `paceFor()` returns a pace (0.5 at 30 s left) and draws the tick. Impact: one minute.

**Suggested change:** Use `spanMs: windowSpanMs(String(title || "") !== "" ? String(title).split(" ").pop() : label)`, sizing titled windows by their last word.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at e6d9c8e)</summary>

Run from a checkout of the PR head (`e6d9c8e1981cf11d832844ed0bfce84635627bd0`) with `node`, `jq` and `python3` available.

The Claude collector titles a model-scoped five-hour window `<model> Session` and uses that title as the label too (`scoped_window()` and `scoped_limits()` in `bin/omarchy-agent-usage-claude`). The case below adds that shape to the PR's pace block: a `(1M context)` model with 30 seconds left in its session window. It asserts the no-tick result that the PR describes for a misparsed span:

```bash
sed -i "/agents pace is hidden when the parsed span is shorter than the reset/a assertEqual(pace('Opus 5 (1M context) Session', at(30 * 1000), 'Opus 5 (1M context) Session'), -1, 'agents pace stays hidden in the last minute of a misparsed window')" test/shell.d/agent-usage-claude-limits-test.sh
bash test/shell.d/agent-usage-claude-limits-test.sh 2>&1 | tail -4; echo "exit=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
```

Actual output:

```
ok - agents pace is hidden when the parsed span is shorter than the reset
expected: -1
actual:   0.5
not ok - agents pace stays hidden in the last minute of a misparsed window
exit=1
```

`windowSpanMs()` reads the `1M` in the model name as a one-minute window. So `remaining > spanMs` hides the tick only until the last 60 seconds before the reset. In those 60 seconds `paceFor()` returns a value between 0 and 1, and the tick and reset-line pace are drawn from it.
</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified** (sandbox runs at `e6d9c8e` and merged with current `quattro`):
- `paceFor()` gives the expected elapsed share for Claude session and weekly windows, per-model weekly, and Codex `<N>h window` / `<N>m window` / `Weekly (7-day)` labels. It hides the tick for a missing, past or too-distant reset, and for a label with no parsable span such as `Limit`. Balance meters never set `pace`.
- The PR's example reproduces exactly: 87% used with 3d 3h left on a weekly window gives `Resets in 3d 3h · pace 55% (+32 ahead)`.
- In an offscreen QML check of the PR's `Meter` (with `Style` stubbed), the tick moves as `root.nowMs` advances (pace 0.2 → 0.4, x 58 → 118 on a 300 px track), is clamped at the right edge at pace 1, and is hidden at -1.
- The PR merges cleanly with current `quattro`. There, `agent-usage-claude-limits`, `agents-panel` and `qml-text-format` pass.
- The new pace cases fail against the base `Panel.qml`, and the `paceFor()` mutants tried (dropping the span guard, using the remaining share instead of the elapsed share) are caught.

**Optional notes:**
- **Untested inline logic:** mutants that flip the ahead/under sign or move the tick x still pass, because both live in inline bindings. Moving the reset-line composition into a root function (for example `paceText(w)`) would make it testable the way `paceFor()` is.
- **Stale cached usage:** after a failed Claude probe (HTTP 429/5xx or a transport error), the collector serves the cached percent with no status banner, while pace keeps advancing. In a sandbox probe, a cached 78% session read `+38 ahead`, then `-2 under` two hours later with no new data. The verdict's error equals the percent's own staleness and errs optimistic; the staleness predates this PR (see #10616); dropping the ahead/under suffix when `usageStatusText` is set would avoid a drifting verdict once a fallback is flagged.
- **Rounding:** the delta is rounded from unrounded values. With fractional percents it can disagree with the row: at 50.4% used and pace 0.495, the row shows `50%` but the line reads `pace 50% (+1 ahead)`. Using `Math.round(percent * 100) - Math.round(pace * 100)` keeps them consistent.

**Related open PRs:** #13770 conflicts in all three files and replaces `LimitRow` (its new meter has no `pace`). It also appends assertions to the same test file, so the `set -euo pipefail` fix helps there too. #7547's "Available" mode inverts the meter fill, so if both land the tick would need inverting too. #12527 adds day segments to weekly meters in the same `Meter`.
</details>

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source and sandbox tests (plus an offscreen QML check) at `e6d9c8e` and merged with `quattro`; not viewed on a desktop.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
